    What the evidence can tell us

    Documented contribution

    A named person, a specific role and an inspectable source. These claims can enter the existing review system.

    Code similarity

    A comparison of actual code and public implementations. A matching passage is a research lead; check versions, context and license notices.

    Training influence

    Unknown unless supported by separate evidence. Visual resemblance and matching code do not establish which material trained a model.

    One claim. Two source checks.

    The example is a completed, accepted Boids proposal. Investigate a different missing connection rather than resubmitting it.

    The AI reviewers independently check the evidence and scope. Supported additions enter the live catalog. Conflicts, inaccessible sources and uncertain identities stay unresolved. Every decision links back to its sources and submission. AI checks can be wrong; corrections are welcome.

    New techniques begin as sourced records. Animated studies and portraits are added separately.

    Experiments count, too.

    A missing archive does not erase a contribution. Share a prototype, teaching memory or unfinished experiment as an attributed research lead. Evidence levels describe connections, never the importance of a person.

    Review allowance

    Loading the public review ledger…

    At most 40 paid attempts per UTC month and two per contributor per UTC day. Each attempt reserves $0.20 before either of its two bounded AI calls. The $8 monthly allowance leaves $2 below the project’s $10 ceiling. Failed attempts still count. Requests wait when the allowance is used.

    This controls this reviewer, not other OpenAI account usage. Pricing policy expires December 1, 2026; reviews stop until refreshed. How the cap works ↗
